name: Jaazaniah
overview: The name Jaazaniah appears multiple times in Scripture, referring to distinct individuals who played varied roles in Judah's history. Some bearers of the name were leaders aligned with Gedaliah at Mizpah, demonstrating their military involvement (Jeremiah 40:8; 42:1). Others were Rechabites, noted for their familial faithfulness (Jeremiah 35:3). However, certain Jaazanias were associated with idolatry and wicked counsel, as seen in Ezekiel's vision where Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan participates in pagan incense rituals (Ezekiel 8:11), and Jaazaniah the son of Azur is identified as a prince giving evil advice to the people (Ezekiel 11:1-2). These portrayals collectively highlight the complex spiritual and political challenges in Judah prior to exile.
